basis: Chronic bacterial infection; cervicofacial disease with invasive subcutaneous masses, abscesses and fibrosis accounts for ~50-60%. Other organ sites individually fall below 30%.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: invasive cervicofacial soft-tissue disease affects subcutis in roughly 50-60%, causing abscesses and fibrosis.

basis: Lectin-complement immunodeficiency; necrotizing enterocolitis in 2/2 is a separately diagnosed complication. Recurrent infections do not establish intrinsic lung or skin damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: necrotizing enterocolitis occurs in 2/2 annotated patients, but is a separate disease associated with immune deficiency rather than intrinsic bowel involvement.

basis: Benign hepatic vascular tumor defined by cavernous blood-vessel spaces; neither endocrine nor blood-cell disease is established.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: this is a blood-vessel neoplasm with cavernous vascular spaces; its hepatic location also warrants hepatic.

basis: Cardiac and skeletal defects define syndrome; ptosis 16/16 and bleeding 6/17 support involvement. Keratosis pilaris 9/17 omitted at cap in favor of more consequential organ dysfunction.

decisions.ocular: involved: eyelid ptosis occurs in 16/16 annotated patients and represents a persistent structural and functional eyelid defect.
decisions.dermatologic: none at cap: keratosis pilaris occurs in 9/17, but cardiac, skeletal, eyelid and coagulation defects take priority for severity.

basis: Laryngeal adductor paralysis defines persistent upper-airway motor dysfunction. The supplied evidence does not establish a peripheral nerve, neuromuscular junction or CNS lesion.

decisions.neurologic: none: paralysis establishes laryngeal dysfunction, but its neural localization is not established by the record.

basis: Cerebellar degeneration and axonal neuropathy define disease. Muscle atrophy in 2/2 and scoliosis in 1/2 reflect secondary neuromotor effects rather than direct muscle or bone disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle atrophy in 2/2 is attributable to denervation; scoliosis in 1/2 is secondary. Neither establishes direct musculoskeletal pathology.

basis: Hair-follicle inflammation is usually infectious, most often bacterial. The umbrella rule follows the usual infectious phenotype despite inclusion of sterile subtypes.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: most ordinary folliculitis is infectious, usually bacterial; the umbrella rule requires the majority phenotype rather than universal infection.

basis: Inherited PRNP prion disease causes spongiform brain degeneration and dementia in 9/9. Infectious prion propagation supports the mechanism axis despite genetic initiation.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: this is a transmissible prion disease involving infectious prion propagation; hereditary initiation does not remove its prion mechanism.

basis: Hereditary motor neuronopathy; muscle wasting in 30-79% is secondary to denervation rather than direct muscle pathology. Structural foot deformities occur in only 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: frequent muscle atrophy (30-79%) is a denervation consequence, not direct muscle disease; skeletal deformities are occasional (5-29%).

basis: Congenital myopathy, contractures, cerebral and retinal hemorrhages define syndrome. Respiratory insufficiency in 3/3 reflects neuromuscular failure rather than direct airway or lung disease.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory insufficiency in 3/3 results from severe neuromuscular weakness; direct pulmonary pathology is not established.
